newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Tuesday December 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Tuesday December 10.

text.p: The following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* Lower house and upper house (Senate) chairmen Luciano Violante and Nicola Mancino are due to meet with president Oscar Luigi Scalfaro to discuss the "justice emergency" after controversial developments in the enquiry involving former magistrate and Public Works minister Antonio Di Pietro (all).

* New documents in a police report leaked to the press allege a complex relationship between banker Pierfrancesco Pacini Battaglia, recently jailed in a corruption probe, and friends of Antonio Di Pietro (Corriere della Sera).

* The centre-right opposition political bloc will decide today its attitude over the 1997 budget examination in the upper house. The centre-right alliance left the lower house a month ago protesting against measures included in the budget (all).
* Prime minister Romano Prodi says banks should ease interest rates. "This country has the right to benefit from lowering inflation" (all).
* In an interview, Prodi answers to criticism from Italy's industrial association Confindustria: "They attack me, but markets promote my policy" (La Stampa).

* Bank of Italy governor Antonio Fazio says the bank is closely watching domestic inflation figures and that in a few weeks time data will show if the consumer price inflation (CPI) is heading in the right direction. Fazio also says CPI in 1996 is averaging 3.8 percent (all).
* Fiat warned at an meeting of its top managers that 1996 had been a difficult year and that the group did not see major improvements in its markets for 1997 (all).
* State industrial holding IRI is expected to discuss today in a general meeting the transfer of its 63.2 percent stake in STET to the Treasury (Il Sole 24 Ore).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
